checks.number_reputation: The phone number's reputation check didn't complete
checks.sender_authentication: ApolloSG couldn't read the email's sender authentication (SPF, DKIM and DMARC)

failures.quota_exhausted: its lookup allowance is used up for now
failures.unsafe_destination: it pointed somewhere Apollo won't connect to
failures.original_not_provided: ApolloSG received a copy of the email without its full headers

completeness.stale: the live lookup failed ({failure}), so Apollo used the result of its last check

failureSentences.quota_exhausted: The service's lookup allowance is used up for now.
failureSentences.rejected: The service couldn't accept the request.
failureSentences.malformed: The service's answer couldn't be read.
failureSentences.not_configured: This check isn't set up here.
failureSentences.unsafe_destination: The link pointed somewhere Apollo won't connect to.
failureSentences.redirect_limit: The link redirected too many times.
failureSentences.original_not_provided: ApolloSG didn't receive the full email headers.
failureSentences.not_recorded: The receiving mail server didn't record those results in the email.

evidenceNames.destinations: Reputation of the places it connects to
evidenceNames.pwa_origin: Website the installed web app came from

statuses.recorded: Recorded by the source, not verified by ApolloSG

evidenceProfiles.signalsTitle: Investigation signals — not proof of fraud
evidenceProfiles.caution: Each of these is one signal to weigh in context. On its own, none of them makes something safe or fraudulent.
evidenceProfiles.authCaution: Passing SPF, DKIM or DMARC confirms only which domain sent the email. It never makes an email safe.

email.label: Email

L1.label: L1 — Visual/Text
L1.received: a screenshot or pasted text of the email
L1.basis: ApolloSG only received a screenshot or pasted text, so technical sender authentication could not be independently verified.

L2.label: L2 — Shared Email
L2.received: the email shared from another app, with the details that app passed on
L2.basis: ApolloSG received the email shared from another app, but not its full headers, so technical sender authentication could not be independently verified.

L3.label: L3 — Original Message
L3.received: the original email with its full headers
L3.basis: ApolloSG examined the original email and full headers.

L4.label: L4 — Provider-Verified Source
L4.received: the original email, retrieved by ApolloSG itself through your connected email account
L4.basis: ApolloSG retrieved the original email itself through your connected email account and examined it with its full headers.

via.connected_mailbox: Retrieved from your connected email account

email.authRecorded: Recorded by {server}, the mail server that received this email. ApolloSG reports this result as recorded and didn't re-check it.
email.authUnconfirmed: Recorded in the email by {server}. ApolloSG couldn't match that to the servers that delivered it, and didn't re-check it.
email.authNotRecorded: The receiving mail server didn't record a result for this.
email.authNeedsOriginal: Needs the original email with its full headers.
email.upgrade: Evidence upgraded from {from} to {to}. Higgins Triage re-checked the email with the new evidence; the earlier result is kept in the case history.
email.upgradeMismatch: That original doesn't match the email you checked, so ApolloSG checked it as a separate email.

signals.reply_to_differs: Replies would go to {replyTo}, not the sender's domain {from}.
signals.return_path_differs: Bounced mail goes to {returnPath}, a different domain from the sender {from}. Mailing services often do this.
signals.spf_failed: The receiving server recorded SPF as {result}: the server that sent it wasn't authorised to send for {domain}.
signals.dkim_failed: The receiving server recorded DKIM as {result}: the email's signature didn't check out.
signals.dmarc_failed: The receiving server recorded DMARC as {result}: the email didn't prove it really came from {from}.
signals.dkim_unaligned: The DKIM signature that passed belongs to {domain}, not the sender's domain {from}.
signals.no_auth_recorded: The receiving mail server didn't record any SPF, DKIM or DMARC results in this email.
signals.recorder_unconfirmed: The authentication results were recorded by {server}, which ApolloSG couldn't match to the servers that delivered this email.
signals.display_name_address: The sender's display name shows the address {shown}, but the email was sent from {from}.
signals.message_id_differs: Its Message-ID was created at {domain}, not at the sender's domain {from}.

link.label: Link or website

as_given.label: Link as given
as_given.basis: ApolloSG only had the link itself — none of its lookups answered, so nothing about the site could be verified.

checked.label: Link checked
checked.received: the link, checked against ApolloSG's lookups
checked.basis: ApolloSG checked the link with its own lookups.

followed.label: Destination followed
followed.received: the link, followed by ApolloSG to where it really leads
followed.basis: ApolloSG followed the link to its final destination and checked it there.

seen_by_site_gate.label: Connection seen by Site Gate
seen_by_site_gate.received: a connection this phone tried to make, seen by Site Gate
seen_by_site_gate.basis: ApolloSG's Site Gate saw this phone try to connect to the site and stopped it on this device. It saw where the connection was going, not the page itself.

via.message: Link from a message or email

notes.noLookup: ApolloSG's lookups didn't answer, so this couldn't be checked.
notes.notFollowed: ApolloSG couldn't follow the link to where it finally leads.
notes.followedBy: Followed by ApolloSG's server. It never opens the page on your phone.
notes.registry: Recorded by the domain's registry, not verified by ApolloSG.
notes.reputation: Each list says only what it already knows. A clean answer isn't proof that a site is safe.
notes.tls: ApolloSG doesn't inspect the site's security certificate.
notes.hosting: ApolloSG doesn't look up where the site is hosted.
notes.siteGateOnly: Site Gate sees the site's name, not the full link or the page.
notes.connectionSeen: Seen by ApolloSG's Site Gate on this phone.
notes.blockConfirmed: Blocked on this phone, confirmed by the operating system.
notes.blockFlow: The operating system reported the connection as stopped.

link.upgrade: Evidence upgraded from {from} to {to}. Higgins Triage re-checked the link with it; the earlier result is kept in the case history.
link.recheck: Higgins Triage re-checked the link with fresh lookups. The earlier result is kept in the case history.
link.recheckWeaker: The re-check couldn't get as far as the earlier check ({level}), so this case keeps its earlier result.

signals.redirects_elsewhere: The link redirects to {final}, a different site from {host}.
signals.destination_unverified: ApolloSG couldn't follow the link to where it finally leads, so the page it opens wasn't checked.

message.label: Message

screenshot.label: Screenshot
screenshot.basis: ApolloSG only received a screenshot, so who really sent it and when could not be verified.

pasted.label: Pasted text
pasted.basis: ApolloSG only received the pasted text, so who really sent it and when could not be verified.

shared.label: Shared from an app
shared.received: the message shared from another app
shared.basis: ApolloSG received the message shared from another app; the app passed on its text, not proof of who sent it.

captured.label: Captured from the notification
captured.received: the message as your phone's notification showed it
captured.basis: ApolloSG read the message from your phone's notification itself, so it knows which app posted it and when — not who really sent it.

inbox.label: Read from your messages
inbox.received: the message as your phone's messages app stored it
inbox.basis: ApolloSG read the message from your phone's messages, so it knows the number or name it arrived from and when — not who really sent it.

notes.senderAsShown: As shown in the message. A sender name or number can be faked.
notes.senderStored: As your phone stored it. A sender name or number can still be faked.
notes.senderMissing: ApolloSG wasn't told who sent it.
notes.timeMissing: ApolloSG wasn't given when it arrived.
notes.sourceKnown: ApolloSG knows how it received this message.
notes.screenshotText: Read from the screenshot on this phone; text the picture didn't show couldn't be read.
notes.provenance: Messaging apps don't share who really sent a message, so ApolloSG can't verify it.
notes.provenanceProvider: {provider} shared its own rating of this sender. That's its rating, not proof of who sent it.
notes.linksChecked: Each link was checked with ApolloSG's lookups.
notes.linksPartly: {failed} of {total} links couldn't be checked: ApolloSG's lookups didn't answer.
notes.numbersChecked: Each number was checked with ApolloSG's number-reputation lookup.
notes.numbersPartly: {failed} of {total} numbers couldn't be checked: the reputation lookup didn't answer.
notes.noNumbers: The message has no phone numbers.
notes.attachments: Only the text reached ApolloSG. Pictures or files sent with the message didn't.

message.upgrade: Evidence upgraded from {from} to {to}. Higgins Triage re-checked the message with it; the earlier result is kept in the case history.
message.recheck: Higgins Triage re-checked the message. The earlier result is kept in the case history.

signals.platform_switch: It asks you to move the conversation to another app or number.
signals.new_number: The sender says they have a new number.
signals.callback_number: It gives a number to call ({number}). Use a number you already know instead.
signals.links_unchecked: ApolloSG couldn't check {count} of its links.
signals.numbers_unchecked: ApolloSG couldn't check {count} of its phone numbers.
signals.brand_without_link: It claims to be {brand} but gives no official way to check it.

call.label: Call

number_only.label: Number only
number_only.basis: ApolloSG only had the number; its reputation lookup didn't answer, so nothing about it could be verified.

number_checked.label: Number checked
number_checked.received: the phone number, checked with a number-reputation lookup
number_checked.basis: ApolloSG checked the number's reputation. The number shown for a call can be faked, and ApolloSG can't yet read the phone network's own caller verification.

screened_call.label: Call screened by ApolloSG
screened_call.received: the call itself, seen by ApolloSG's call screening
screened_call.basis: ApolloSG's call screening saw this call arrive. The number shown can still be faked, and ApolloSG can't yet read the phone network's own caller verification.

described.label: Described by you
described.received: the call as you described it
described.basis: ApolloSG only had what you told it about the call, so who really called could not be verified.

notes.numberShown: The number shown for a call can be faked.
notes.callerId: ApolloSG can't yet read the phone network's own caller verification.
notes.timeScreened: Seen by ApolloSG's call screening on this phone.
notes.timeMissing: ApolloSG didn't see the call itself, only {what}.
notes.screening: ApolloSG's call screening on this phone saw the call arrive.
notes.noScreening: ApolloSG's call screening didn't see this call.
notes.recorded: Recorded by the number-reputation service, not verified by ApolloSG.
notes.notLookedUp: ApolloSG doesn't look the number up for a described call. Check the number to add this.
notes.stale: The lookup failed this time, so this is the last answer from {date}.
notes.spoofing: From the line type and reputation. A faked caller ID can't be ruled out.

call.upgrade: Evidence upgraded from {from} to {to}. Higgins Triage re-checked the number with it; the earlier result is kept in the case history.
call.recheck: Higgins Triage re-checked the number. The earlier result is kept in the case history.

signals.voip: It's an internet (VOIP) number. These are easy to get and often used to fake caller ID.
signals.recent_abuse: Others have recently reported this number for abuse.
signals.invalid: It isn't a valid, active phone number.
signals.carrier_warning: You said your carrier warned about this call.
signals.remote_ask: The caller asked you to install an app, share your screen or give remote access.
signals.secret_ask: The caller asked for a code, password or card details.
signals.brand_claim: The caller said they were from {brand}. Anyone can say that on a call.

name_only.label: File name only
name_only.basis: ApolloSG couldn't read the file's contents, so it could only go by the name and size.

contents_read.label: Contents read
contents_read.received: the file, read on your phone
contents_read.basis: ApolloSG read the start of the file on your phone to find what it really is.

fingerprinted.label: Contents read and fingerprinted
fingerprinted.received: the whole file, read and fingerprinted on your phone
fingerprinted.basis: ApolloSG read the file on your phone, found what it really is and fingerprinted it (SHA-256).

notes.byName: Taken from the file's name. A name is only a claim.
notes.byApp: Supplied by the app it came from. Only a claim.
notes.trueType: Read from the file's first bytes on this phone.
notes.notRead: ApolloSG couldn't read the file's contents{reason}.
notes.sha: Calculated on this phone from the whole file. The file isn't uploaded.
notes.shaNotWhole: ApolloSG read only the start of the file, so it couldn't fingerprint it.
notes.metadata: ApolloSG doesn't read document metadata yet.
notes.signature: ApolloSG doesn't check a file's signatures or certificates yet.
notes.macroFormat: Its format can run macros. ApolloSG doesn't open them.
notes.noMacroFormat: ApolloSG doesn't look inside documents for macros.
notes.links: Only the part ApolloSG read was searched.
notes.threats: ApolloSG doesn't compare files with malware lists yet.

signals.type_mismatch: Its name says {claimed}, but it's really {real}.
signals.double_extension: Its name hides a second extension: {name}.
signals.hidden_characters: Its name uses hidden characters to disguise its real extension.
signals.executable: It's a program or script, not a document.
signals.installer: It installs an app or changes device settings.
signals.archive_password: A password came with the archive. That's often used to get past scanners.
signals.macros: It can run macros when it's opened.

image.label: Image
image.basis: ApolloSG read the picture on your phone. A picture shows what was on screen, not where it came from.

capabilities.embedded_identifiers: Links, numbers and codes in it

notes.content: Read on this phone. A picture shows what was on screen, not where it came from.
notes.noText: ApolloSG couldn't read any text in it.
notes.metadata: Removed on this phone before anything was sent. ApolloSG doesn't use it as evidence.
notes.source: ApolloSG knows how it received the picture, not where the picture came from.
notes.identifiers: Found in the picture's text and checked with ApolloSG's lookups.

signals.redacted: It showed sensitive details, which ApolloSG blacked out before sending it.
signals.flagged: {count} of the links, numbers or codes in it looked suspicious.

decoded.label: QR payload decoded
decoded.received: the QR code, decoded by ApolloSG
decoded.basis: ApolloSG decoded the QR code itself, so it knows exactly what the code contains — not who put it there.

described.label: Described by you
described.basis: ApolloSG only had the details you entered, so the app's real identity, source and permissions could not be verified.

read_from_device.label: Read from this device
read_from_device.received: the installed app's details, read from this phone
read_from_device.basis: ApolloSG read the installed app's details from this phone. Its signing information isn't available to ApolloSG yet.

via.picked: Installed app chosen on this phone

notes.permissions: Requested by the app, as this phone's system records it.
notes.permissionsTicked: As you ticked them. ApolloSG couldn't read the app's real permissions.
notes.notRead: ApolloSG couldn't read this app's details from this phone.
notes.signing: Signing information isn't available to ApolloSG yet.
notes.store: ApolloSG can't read the app store's or the phone's own security checks.
notes.version: ApolloSG doesn't read the app's version yet.

signals.sideloaded: It wasn't installed from an official app store.
signals.remote_access: It can see or control your screen.
signals.accessibility: It has accessibility access, which can read what's on your screen.
signals.overlay: It can draw over other apps.
signals.notifications: It can read your notifications, including codes sent by text.
signals.brand_name: Its name mentions {brand}. Check that's really who made it.
signals.bad_destination: It connects to {count} address{plural} with a malicious reputation.

coverageGapCodes.plain: This device doesn't make that information available to ApolloSG.
ApolloSG needs a permission before it can complete this check.
A reputation service didn't answer in time.
ApolloSG couldn't reach the network to complete this check.
The content couldn't be opened for inspection.
Apollo can't inspect this kind of file.
The contents are encrypted, so Apollo couldn't inspect them.
The technical sender information wasn't available.
